subject.title: Discord DMs: inbound messages silently dropped (outbound works)

question: Should Discord root `allowFrom` be an additive global allowlist for every account, or should account-scoped `allowFrom` remain a restrictive override that only inherits root when unset?
rationale: The obvious repair for the reporter broadens who can DM account-scoped bots, so automation should not choose the authorization contract without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Preserve restrictive account overrides
options.body: Keep account `allowFrom` as the limiting scope when set, and fix the user pain through effective-allowlist diagnostics, docs, status, and live-proofed routing guidance.

options.title: Make root allowFrom additive
options.body: Merge root and account `allowFrom` for Discord accounts, accepting that existing account-restricted bots may become reachable by globally allowlisted users.

options.title: Add an explicit inheritance mode
options.body: Introduce a documented, migrated policy knob for additive versus restrictive account allowlists, at the cost of new config surface and upgrade complexity.

recommendation.title: Preserve restrictive account overrides
recommendation.body: Keep account `allowFrom` as the limiting scope when set, and fix the user pain through effective-allowlist diagnostics, docs, status, and live-proofed routing guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent Discord DM access and shared allowlist resolver history points to steipete as the best available routing owner for this security-sensitive contract choice.
